title.value: Inferring disease subtypes from clusters in explanation space
title.justification: The title 'Inferring disease subtypes from clusters in explanation space' is directly mentioned at the top of the research paper, representing the main focus of the paper as it explores the clustering approach in the explanation space to identify disease subtypes.
title.quote:
Inferring disease subtypes
from clusters in explanation space

analysis.description: This paper introduces a novel approach for discovering latent disease subtypes by analyzing instance-wise explanations of a diagnostic classifier's decisions, rather than the original dataset features. The approach is compared to classical clustering on various datasets, showing improved subtype recovery in explanation space.

type.justification: The paper is empirical as it conducts experiments on multiple datasets, including UK Biobank brain imaging data and Cancer Genome Atlas data, to demonstrate the efficacy of clustering in explanation space for disease subtype discovery.
type.quote:
In multiple datasets with
known ground-truth subclasses, particularly on UK Biobank brain imaging data and transcriptome
data from the Cancer Genome Atlas, we show that cluster analysis on model explanations
substantially outperforms the classical approach.

name.justification: The focus of the paper is on improving clinical diagnosis and treatment selection by identifying disease subtypes, which falls under the domain of Precision Medicine.
name.quote: Identification of disease subtypes and corresponding biomarkers can substantially improve clinical diagnosis and treatment selection.

name.justification: The paper utilizes instance-wise explanations from a diagnostic classifier, essentially leveraging explainable AI to create an explanation space for better subtype discovery.
name.quote: Recent interest in explaining the output of complex machine learning models has been characterized by a wide range of approaches, most of them focused on providing an instance-wise explanation of a model’s output.

name.justification: The paper employs clustering methods on the explanation space to discover disease subtypes, emphasizing the use of clustering techniques.
name.quote: The search for biologically grounded subtypes is frequently carried out by means of cluster analysis to identify groups of subjects with similar disease phenotypes.

name.justification: The analysis of biomedical datasets, such as UK Biobank brain imaging and Cancer Genome Atlas data, for disease subtypes classifies the paper's sub-field as Biomedical Data Analysis.
name.quote: In both the Cancer Genome Atlas and the UK Biobank brain imaging data, task-conditioned explanations proved to be highly informative.

name.justification: The paper explicitly mentions the use of a Random Forest classifier for transforming feature space into explanation space through Shapley Additive Explanations.
name.quote: A Random Forest ­classifier was trained on the binary classification problem and SHapley Additive Explana­tions (SHAP) were used to generate instance-wise explanations for the predictions of the classifier.

is_contributed.justification: The Random Forest classifier is a widely known model outside the scope of this paper, thus it is not a contribution of the paper.
is_contributed.quote: A Random Forest ­classifier was trained on the binary classification problem and SHapley Additive Explana­tions (SHAP) were used to generate instance-wise explanations for the predictions of the classifier.

is_executed.justification: The Random Forest classifier is used in the empirical study conducted in the paper, demonstrating its execution.
is_executed.quote: A Random Forest ­classifier was trained on the binary classification problem and SHapley Additive Explana­tion (SHAP) were used to generate instance-wise explanations for the predictions of the classifier.

is_compared.justification: The Random Forest classifier itself is not compared numerically, but rather the clusters resulting from using the classifier's explanation space are compared with those from feature space.
is_compared.quote: We compare our ability to recover subtypes via cluster analysis on model explanations to classical cluster analysis on the original data.

referenced_paper_title.justification: The reference to Breiman, L. in the context of Random Forest indicates this is related to the foundational paper 'Random forests'.
referenced_paper_title.quote: Breiman, L. Random forests. Mach. Learn. 45(1), 5–32 (2001).
